author: Role 2 (Trust Engine Engineer)
description: Proposed physical measurement noise model for stability assessment (E8), sensitivity curves, and calibration robustness testing (E4). All values are initial simulation proposals awaiting formal review and confirmation with Role 1 (ML Lead).

N.name: Nitrogen
N.rationale: Field soil testing kits and extraction variance typically exhibit 5-15% lab uncertainty. Relative scaling reflects proportional dilution errors, with a 2.0 kg/ha additive floor preventing zero variance at the boundary.

P.name: Phosphorus
P.rationale: Bray/Olsen extraction methods vary across soil testing facilities; +/-10% reflects standard lab variance. Additive floor of 2.0 kg/ha ensures near-zero concentrations remain perturbed.

K.name: Potassium
K.rationale: Flame photometry extraction methods exhibit 5-10% coefficient of variation. Physical upper bound accommodates high-potassium crops (grapes/apples).

temperature.name: Temperature
temperature.rationale: Microclimate differences between canopy level and nearby weather stations commonly range from 1.0 to 2.0 deg C. Interval scale requires absolute additive noise rather than percentage.

humidity.name: Humidity
humidity.rationale: Commercial capacitive hygrometers exhibit typical drift of +/-3 to +/-5 percentage points. Absolute additive noise prevents unrealistic suppression of error at low relative humidity.

ph.name: pH
ph.rationale: Field glass electrodes and test strips vary by +/-0.2 to 0.3 units due to soil slurry dilution and temperature. Because pH is logarithmic, absolute noise represents a factor-of-two ion concentration variance.

rainfall.name: Rainfall
rainfall.rationale: Spatial precipitation variability across a farm gauge network typically exhibits 10-15% variation. Additive floor of 5.0 mm prevents near-zero rainfall periods from having zero uncertainty.
